clue.text: Gives up dessert to get moving

parts.note: to kick a habit is to give it up, so gives up means kicks
a tart is a sweet pastry served as a dessert

explanation.surface: Someone skips pudding in order to get going again.
explanation.definitionFit: To kick-start an engine or a project is to set it going, as with a motorcycle's kick pedal.

clue.text: Done for king — a tender

parts.note: K is the chess and card abbreviation for king
to tender a proposal is to put it forward, so tender means put

explanation.surface: A ruined monarch is described alongside a gentle carer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tender' looks like an adjective (gentle) or a noun (a railway wagon) but is a verb: to put forward.
explanation.definitionFit: Kaput is German-derived slang for broken or finished, the same as done for.

clue.text: Bill (from America) and wife make final move

parts.note: in American English a restaurant bill is a check
a mate is a spouse or partner, here a wife

explanation.surface: A couple settle the restaurant bill and leave as the last thing they do.
explanation.definitionFit: Checkmate is the move that ends a chess game, so it is the last move played.

clue.text: Equine disease kills

definitions.meaning: a contagious bacterial infection of horses, affecting the throat
throttles someone to death by squeezing the neck

explanation.definitionFit: The horse illness takes its name from the choking it causes, and the verb means throttles fatally.

clue.text: Lawman arousing real anger? Not yet

indicators.note: arousing means stirring up, so these letters are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: A legal official is stirring up fury that has not yet come.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark and 'Not yet' look like comment on the anger but are anagram fodder, rearranged with REAL ANGER.
explanation.definitionFit: The Attorney General is the chief law officer of the government, so a lawman in the broad sense.

clue.text: Ocean-going tug, one that can be relied upon?

definitions.meaning: read whimsically, a powerful vessel that tows: a tower of great strength

definitions.text: one that can be relied upon?
definitions.meaning: a dependable person who gives support in a crisis

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom names a reliable supporter, and taken literally it describes a strong boat that tows ships.

clue.text: Southern Scotland's extended, in a manner of speaking

parts.note: lang is the Scots word for long, meaning extended

explanation.surface: Someone notes that the south of Scotland has been stretched, figuratively speaking.
explanation.walkthrough: LANG is the Scottish form of long, as in auld lang syne.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang is an informal kind of vocabulary, a particular way of talking.

clue.text: Lots of sense

definitions.meaning: informally, a ... of something means a great deal of it, as in a ... better
one of the five senses, vision

explanation.definitionFit: Vision is one of the five senses, and colloquially a sight means a large amount.

clue.text: Leader elected for a further term

parts.note: an aga is a commander or chief in the Ottoman Empire
a candidate voted into office is in

explanation.surface: A political leader wins re-election to serve another term of office.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a re-elected leader, but AGA is an old Turkish title for a commander.
explanation.definitionFit: Again means once more, as when something happens for another round or time.

clue.text: Bravery displayed by everyone in stand

indicators.note: in tells us one word sits inside the other

parts.note: a gantry is a frame or stand, for barrels or for cranes
all means everyone

explanation.surface: Courage is on show from the whole crowd in the grandstand.
explanation.definitionFit: Gallantry is courage, especially in battle, as in medals awarded for it.

clue.text: White-faced player makes one blunder in Crucible

indicators.note: in says the blunder goes inside the vessel

parts.note: a crucible is a pot for melting metal
I is the Roman numeral for one
to err is to make a mistake

explanation.surface: A snooker player in white make-up makes a mistake at the Crucible.
explanation.walkthrough: The Crucible is the Sheffield theatre where the world snooker championship is played, which makes 'player' look like a snooker player.
explanation.definitionFit: Pierrot is the sad clown of French pantomime, whose face is painted white.

clue.text: Bird dog may, when happy

definitions.meaning: a small songbird that bobs its long tail
read as a phrase, what a pleased dog does with its rear end

explanation.definitionFit: The bird is named for its constantly bobbing tail, and a pleased dog moves its tail the same way.

clue.text: Stolen from market -a kennel

indicators.note: from tells us the answer is lifted out of the run of letters that follows

explanation.surface: A dog was stolen from a kennel at the market.
explanation.definitionFit: Something taken has been seized or stolen.

clue.text: Hope invention brings game girl new top-class backing

parts.note: RU is rugby union
Rita is a girl's name

indicators.note: backing means the word for top-class is read backwards

parts.note: A1 is first class; read as letters, AI

explanation.surface: Hope is placed in an invented game for girls that is new and first-rate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hope' is Anthony Hope, author of The Prisoner of Zenda, not the feeling.
explanation.definitionFit: Anthony Hope created the fictional central European kingdom in The Prisoner of Zenda.

clue.text: Stroke fawn

definitions.meaning: as a verb, to fawn is to grovel obsequiously

explanation.definitionFit: Front crawl is a swimming stroke, and to grovel or toady is to behave servilely.

clue.text: Lines to face — a hundred lines and parts of lines

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred
rows are lines, as of seats
metrical feet are the units that make up lines of verse

explanation.surface: Someone gets a punishment of a hundred lines, plus bits of others.
explanation.walkthrough: FEET are the units of rhythm in poetry, so lines of verse are made of them.
explanation.definitionFit: Crow's feet are the wrinkles at the outer corners of the eyes.

clue.text: Capable of resolving tiff with niece

indicators.note: resolving means sorting out, so these letters are reworked

explanation.surface: Someone is good at patching up a quarrel with their niece.
explanation.definitionFit: Efficient describes someone competent who gets things done well.

clue.text: Assembling from various sources a light meal

definitions.meaning: gathering and comparing material from different places
a cold buffet or snack, especially in old usage

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both gathering texts together and a light repast.

clue.text: Make-up of bride more elaborate

indicators.note: make-up here is composition, so these letters are made up into a new order

explanation.surface: A bride's cosmetics are made more ornate.
explanation.definitionFit: To embroider a story is to embellish it with added detail.

clue.text: Give short change in error

indicators.note: change tells us the letters are switched around

explanation.surface: Someone hands over too little change by mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short change' looks like a phrase about cheating, but 'change' is the anagram signal on GIVE SHORT.
explanation.definitionFit: An oversight is a slip or mistake made through not noticing.

clue.text: Try to exert pressure by coming in behind high shot

indicators.note: coming in behind says the second word follows the high shot

parts.note: a lob is a high looping shot in tennis

explanation.surface: A tennis player tries to pressurise by running in after a lob.
explanation.definitionFit: To lobby is to campaign to influence those in power.

clue.text: Significance of warship taking position

parts.note: a sub is a submarine, a war vessel
a stance is a position or posture

explanation.surface: A warship's importance in taking up position is stated.
explanation.definitionFit: Substance means real importance or weight, as in an argument of little substance.

clue.text: Man, perhaps, putting gym in order

indicators.note: in tells us one piece sits inside another

parts.note: a bid is an order or command
PE, physical education, is school gym

explanation.surface: Someone arranges gym equipment neatly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in order' reads as tidy; split, 'in' is the container signal and 'order' is BID.
explanation.definitionFit: A biped walks on two feet, and a human is an example.

clue.text: Stay black

definitions.meaning: covered in or like pitch, dark as tar

explanation.definitionFit: The verb means linger, and the adjective means coated with dark pitch.

clue.text: Throughout a marathon

parts.note: a marathon session is a very long one

explanation.surface: Something lasts for the entire length of a long-distance race.
explanation.definitionFit: Along can mean all the way through, as in all along.

clue.text: Information about hidden place for putting pills

indicators.note: hidden says one word is concealed inside the other

parts.note: gen is British slang for information
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: A tip-off reveals a secret stash where drugs are kept.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pills' suggests drugs, but it is old slang for balls; the putting green is where golf balls are putted.
explanation.definitionFit: On a golf course, the green is the area where balls are putted into the hole.

clue.text: Ancient city, about to welcome a ruler

indicators.note: to welcome means to take in, so the city holds the next piece
about means the city is turned round

parts.note: Rome is the city of the ancient Roman world
a means per, as in five pounds a head

explanation.surface: An old city is about to receive a monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about to' reads as 'on the point of'; in fact 'about' turns the city round and 'to welcome' makes it hold the next piece, with 'a' meaning per as in prices quoted per item.
explanation.definitionFit: An emperor is a sovereign of an empire.

clue.text: Cook needing good sieve

parts.note: a riddle is a coarse sieve for soil or gravel

explanation.surface: A chef needs a decent strainer.
explanation.definitionFit: To griddle food is to cook it on a flat iron plate.

clue.text: Extremely tipsy, having imbibed rum — a strong drink

indicators.note: having imbibed means taking another piece inside
extremely means the outside letters of the next word

parts.note: rum means odd or strange

explanation.surface: A very drunk person who has had rum has a strong drink.
explanation.walkthrough: The outside letters of 'tipsy' are T and Y, around ODD.
explanation.definitionFit: A toddy is a hot drink of spirits, water, sugar and spice.

clue.text: Opera set, oddly, in Leghorn

indicators.note: oddly says these letters are arranged in an odd way

explanation.surface: An opera is staged, strangely, in the Italian port of Leghorn.
explanation.walkthrough: Leghorn is the old English name for Livorno.
explanation.definitionFit: Lohengrin is Wagner's romantic opera about the swan knight.
